subject: [PATCH 0/2] mm: refactor zonelist constructors and iterators

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged a missing Ack from Balbir Singh and added it to the patch
reviews.raw_body:
Just realized this should carry an Ack from Balbir

Acked-by: Balbir Singh <balbirs@nvidia.com>

see - https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/62bf02dc-dab1-41bf-8204-eb3566628b93@nvidia.com/

2026-09-02.patch_summary: This patch refactors the zonelist constructors and iterators in the Linux kernel to make them more flexible and modular. The changes include extracting a new function `find_next_best_node_in` that takes an explicit candidate set, and moving the per-node construction loop out of `build_zonelists` into a separate function `build_node_zonelist`. These changes allow for building zonelists over custom sets of nodes and iterating over them in fallback order. The refactoring is intended to be functional equivalent to the original code, but with improved modularity and flexibility.

reviews.author: Vlastimil (SUSE)
reviews.summary: Reviewer suggested moving pr_cont() printing into build_node_zonelist(), and optionally behind a flag, to avoid passing nr_nodes back to build_zonelists(). They also proposed eliminating the node_order array by processing the loop in build_node_zonelist() itself.
reviews.raw_body:
LGTM, but, while we're at it, could we just do the pr_cont() printing in
build_node_zonelist() itself (maybe behind a flag if you don't want to print
from future new caller) so it doesn't need to pass nr_nodes back to
build_zonelists(). Then also the node_order array could live in
build_node_zonelist() itself?

Actually I wonder if we could get ride of the node_order array completely.
It would mean the loop processing in build_zonelists_in_node_order() would
have to be done piece-meal in build_node_zonelist() itself. But seems
feasible? Depends on how you intend to reuse/extend the new functions later,
I guess...

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges that further testing is needed to determine the generalizability of the patch's changes and does not commit to a fix or timeline.
reviews.raw_body:
I can take a look.  We've been testing a couple different things, will
see how well things generalize (private node fallback lists, inverted
fallback lists for proactive reclaim node ordering, some other stuff).

~Gregory
